name: Flucloxacillin
route_note: Oral capsules/solution (taken on an empty stomach) or IV/IM injection. Not marketed in the United States.

discovery.note: One of the isoxazolyl penicillins (with oxacillin, cloxacillin and dicloxacillin) designed to resist staphylococcal penicillinase.

tagline: Anti-staphylococcal penicillin used widely in the UK, Europe and Australia
summary: Flucloxacillin is a narrow-spectrum, penicillinase-stable penicillin used mainly for infections caused by methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus and streptococci. It is a standard agent for cellulitis and staphylococcal bacteraemia outside North America.
mechanism: Flucloxacillin inhibits penicillin-binding proteins and thereby bacterial cell-wall cross-linking.

A bulky isoxazolyl side chain sterically hinders hydrolysis by staphylococcal beta-lactamase (penicillinase). It is inactive against MRSA, whose PBP2a (encoded by mecA) has low affinity for most beta-lactams, and has little Gram-negative activity.
uses: Skin and soft-tissue infections such as cellulitis, impetigo and wound infections
Methicillin-susceptible S. aureus bacteraemia, endocarditis and osteomyelitis

history.title: Penicillinase problem
history.detail: Spread of penicillinase-producing S. aureus in hospitals drives the search for stable penicillins; methicillin is launched in 1959–60.

history.title: Isoxazolyl penicillins
history.detail: Beecham develops oxacillin and cloxacillin; flucloxacillin follows later in the decade.

history.title: Clinical introduction
history.detail: Flucloxacillin enters clinical use in Europe around 1970 and becomes the UK standard anti-staphylococcal penicillin.

history.title: Pharmacogenetic link
history.detail: A genome-wide association study identifies HLA-B*57:01 as a major risk factor for flucloxacillin-induced liver injury.

history.title: WHO AWaRe classification
history.detail: The WHO Essential Medicines List begins grouping antibiotics into Access, Watch and Reserve categories; cloxacillin (with flucloxacillin as an alternative) is placed in the Access group.

serious: Cholestatic hepatitis, which may appear weeks after stopping and is linked to HLA-B*57:01
High-anion-gap metabolic acidosis (pyroglutamic acidosis) with concomitant paracetamol in at-risk patients

facts: Genome-wide association studies linked flucloxacillin liver injury to the HLA-B*57:01 allele, the same allele that predicts abacavir hypersensitivity.
WHO's Essential Medicines List names cloxacillin, with flucloxacillin and other isoxazolyl penicillins as therapeutic alternatives.
